text:
lisa (support): hey team, just got a customer report — google oauth login failing for a handful of users, they see `PKCE state mismatch` after coming back from accounts.google.com. happens on Chrome 115 and Safari, both on mobile and desktop. they pasted the error: 'invalid_grant: PKCE state mismatch'

carla (engineer): thanks lisa — can you paste the exact callback url the client is sending and the redirect_uri configured in our console? also any repro steps?

lisa (support): repro steps from customer: 1) click 'Sign in with Google' on app 2) redirect to accounts.google.com 3) auth completes, redirect back to `https://app.example.com/auth/callback` 4) page shows auth error and no session. they said sometimes the callback includes a trailing slash: `https://app.example.com/auth/callback/` — app config has `https://app.example.com/auth/callback` (no trailing slash) in the OAuth client settings. they also attached a devtools network snapshot showing the callback params: `?code=4/0AX4XfW...&state=CF-xyz`

carla (engineer): that trailing slash difference can matter depending on our exact matching logic. also PKCE/state mismatch usually means the server couldn't find the state saved in the browser session/cookie when the callback returned. a few quick things to check: 
- Is the state stored in a cookie or localStorage? (cookies need correct SameSite/Path)
- Did we recently change cookie path or remove `httpOnly`?
- Are there any redirects between subdomains that clear cookies?

lisa (support): customer says we store state in a cookie named `_ri_state`. they see the cookie set on the initial redirect but after the redirect back the cookie is gone. attached screenshot shows cookie with `SameSite=Lax` and `Secure` set.

maria (identity): i just pulled the deploy log — deploy-bot shows a config rollout last night that changed our auth cookie path to `/` from `/auth` and added a lightweight proxy rule for the callback to strip a trailing slash. deploy-bot:

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: rollout 2026-11-01T03:12:04Z — feature/auth-callback-normalize deployed to prod (id: fea-492)

maria (identity): so we removed the strict path but ALSO changed the SameSite attribute to `Lax` from `None` in that PR — that means cross-site POSTs (OAuth redirects) may not include the cookie if the flow counts as cross-site in some browsers. i suspect the state cookie isn't sent on callback in Safari/Chrome due to that.

carla (engineer): yep. PKCE state mismatch error reproduced locally after toggling SameSite to Lax. repro snippet:

```
# simulate auth redirect roundtrip
# 1) initiate oauth -> server sets cookie
curl -i -c cookiejar.txt 'https://auth.example.com/start?provider=google'
# 2) simulate google callback (cross-site redirect)
curl -i -b cookiejar.txt 'https://app.example.com/auth/callback?code=FAKE&state=CF-xyz'
```

when SameSite=None the cookie is sent and state validated, when SameSite=Lax it is dropped for cross-site POST/redirect in some browsers.

lisa (support): the customer also reported intermittent behavior — some users succeed, others fail. could this be due to Chrome same-site heuristics + extensions?

maria (identity): intermittent fits — different browser settings/versions treat top-level cross-site GET vs POST differently. Also note our proxy that strips trailing slash might be doing a 302 which can turn a GET into a cross-site navigation that drops cookies depending on SameSite.

carla (engineer): proposed fix: revert SameSite change (set SameSite=None; Secure; `Path=/auth`), and tighten path handling to not issue extra redirects. short-term rollback should unblock users. long-term: switch to storing PKCE state server-side keyed by a short temporary session (or use a signed state value) so we don't rely on cross-site cookies.

lisa (support): i've escalated to the customer-success team and told them we suspect SameSite is the cause and we're testing a rollback. i asked for console logs and which browser versions fail.

maria (identity): i'm going to roll back the PR to restore SameSite=None and remove the proxy 302. doing a targeted rollback in prod now, will post updates.

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollback completed for fea-492 at 2026-11-01T04:22:11Z — auth cookie SameSite restored to None, proxy 302 removed (canary -> prod)

carla (engineer): follow-up checklist for support: 
- ask customer to clear site data and retry once we confirm rollback.
- if they still fail, ask for a HAR file and browser + extension list.
- collect the failing callback URL (with trailing slash or port) and the `_ri_state` cookie snapshot.
- enable debug logs: set REDWOOD_AUTH_DEBUG=1 and send server logs around the callback time. sample log lines you'd see when state is missing:
```
[auth] INFO Received callback code=4/0AX4XfW... state=CF-xyz
[auth] WARN state cookie `_ri_state` not found, cannot validate state
[auth] ERROR PKCE state mismatch -> reject
```

lisa (support): customer tried after rollback and confirmed sign-in works now for the 3 testers they had. they cleared site data first. one user on older Safari still got the error until they cleared cookies. customer asked if we can make the callback tolerant of a trailing slash.

maria (identity): yes we can accept both with exact-match checks by normalizing incoming redirect_uri server-side (strip trailing slash before lookup) rather than issuing redirects. i'll file a follow-up PR to normalize and add an e2e test for cookie flow.

carla (engineer): i'll update the internal KB with root cause + repro + rollback steps and link to the PR when merged. for now mark this thread as resolved once support confirms the broader customer base is green.

lisa (support): marking resolved for this customer; leaving the thread open for any other affected accounts. thanks all :tada:
